extra.message: The endpoint routed at /ops/pulse/account-sheet-glitch-091/ returns raw exception details to the client: str(exc) contains the user-controlled 'lot_ref' value reflected from request.GET plus the internal server path BASE_EXPORT_DIR, and the response also discloses the exception class name via 'debug_type'. cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: logger.warning() writes the full request body and the value of the Authorization header to the application log. Request bodies and Authorization headers (Bearer tokens, API keys, Basic credentials) are sensitive and must never be logged; anyone with log access can harvest credentials.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: Open redirect: the 'lane' query parameter is passed unsanitized to django.shortcuts.redirect(). An attacker can craft /ops/after/account-return-lane-093/?lane=https://evil.example/ to redirect victims to an arbitrary external site for phishing or credential theft.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: Mass assignment / trusted-attribute tampering: user-supplied 'amount' and 'state' (JSON body, POST or GET) directly overwrite server-side ledger attributes. A negative 'amount' (default -250) bypasses the balance/limit business rule (balance 1200 raised above limit 900), and 'state' can be set to any attacker-chosen value, overriding the server default 'approved'.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: Insecure deserialization: pickle.loads() is called on raw request data (request.body or the 'blob' GET parameter, optionally base64-decoded via 'wrap=b64'). Unpickling attacker-controlled data results in arbitrary code execution on the server.

Mass assignment: workset.update(payload) merges arbitrary user-controlled JSON keys into a trusted server-side object whose defaults are security-relevant (role=viewer, tier=standard, approved=False). The client can override 'role', 'tier' and 'approved' directly, bypassing server-side trust decisions.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: Path traversal in file write: the 'ref' GET parameter is interpolated into a file path (BASE_EXPORT_DIR / f"{ref}.json") without sanitization and then written with target.write_text(). Traversal sequences such as ref=../../etc/cron.d/pwn write attacker-influenced JSON (including 'ssn' and 'card' values taken from the query string) to arbitrary filesystem locations.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: Weak hash: hashlib.md5() is used to derive a digest from a user-supplied phrase. MD5 is a cryptographically broken hash and must not be used for any security purpose; a SHA-2 family algorithm is required.

cwe: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

extra.message: Missing authentication: acct_identity_ping_343 is the only view in partner_console.py with no authentication check at all - no _wrk_gate() call and no @login_required decorator. It is publicly routed at /ops/identity/acct-ping-343/ (crm/core/urls.py:35), so any unauthenticated remote caller can submit 'handle' and 'channel' data which is accepted and reflected back in the response.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: Hard-coded verifier secrets: identity verifier PINs {'north': '4812', 'south': '5930'} are embedded in source code. Anyone with access to the source knows the valid verifiers for the /ops/identity/acct-hint-650/ check and can pass it.

CORS misconfiguration: the response reflects the arbitrary client-supplied Origin header into Access-Control-Allow-Origin and additionally sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. Any origin can therefore issue credentialed cross-origin requests to this endpoint and read the responses.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: Security response headers are actively disabled: the view sets X-XSS-Protection: 0 and an empty Content-Security-Policy header, stripping browser defenses against XSS and clickjacking for this response.

Server-Side Template Injection: the 'fragment' GET parameter is concatenated into a Jinja2 Template string and rendered server-side. An attacker can inject template expressions (e.g. {{ 7*7 }}, or payloads traversing __class__.__mro__ to subprocess) to read server internals or achieve remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: Privilege decision based on a client-controlled value: the 'ops_badge' cookie or 'x-ops-badge' request header is trusted to determine an elevated access lane (badge == 'lead' returns 'lane': 'elevated', 'payroll': 'full', 'casework': 'open'). Any caller can trivially set this cookie/header to 'lead' and obtain the elevated response.

OS command injection: the 'host' GET parameter is concatenated directly into an os.system() shell command ('ping -c 1 ' + host) without sanitization. Shell metacharacters (e.g. '; id', '| cat /etc/passwd', '$(cmd)') allow arbitrary command execution with the server's privileges.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

extra.message: Insecure randomness: the Python 'random' module (Mersenne Twister, predictable and not cryptographically secure) is used to generate a token 'code'. Security-sensitive values must be generated with the 'secrets' module.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG)

extra.message: Path traversal in file write: the 'name' GET parameter is joined to BASE_EXPORT_DIR and request.body is written to the resulting path with target.write_bytes() without any validation. '../' sequences allow writing arbitrary attacker-controlled content to arbitrary filesystem locations (e.g. overwriting source files or planting a cron job).

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: TLS peer certificate verification is disabled: ssl._create_unverified_context() is passed to urllib.request.urlopen(). A man-in-the-middle attacker can impersonate the partner endpoint and intercept or tamper with the response that the application treats as trusted.

Information exposure: the endpoint returns internal environment details to remote callers - the value of the DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE environment variable and the absolute filesystem path of BASE_EXPORT_DIR ('base'), aiding further attacks.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: Broken access control in organization_edit: a customer_contact passes _org_access() for their own organization and the only role check performed (lines 162-164) blocks support agents - customer contacts are never blocked. The UI hides the Edit action and internal fields from customers (crm/templates/crm/organization_detail.html:10,37-44), but a direct POST to /organizations/<pk>/edit/ lets a customer modify internal OrganizationForm fields including plan, status, health_score, account_manager and internal_notes.

Incorrect authorization in document_list: the support-agent queryset includes Q(organization__account_manager__isnull=False), which matches every organization that has any account manager assigned. A support agent therefore lists and reads documents (including internal-visibility ones) of organizations they have no relationship with, instead of only organizations with escalations assigned to them.

IDOR / missing tenant scoping in document_download: for support agents the only restriction is that billing-visibility documents are denied; there is no check that the agent is assigned to the document's organization (contrast User.can_access_organization, crm/accounts/models.py:65-66, which requires an assigned escalation). Any support agent can download internal and customer-visible documents of any organization by requesting /documents/<uuid>/download/.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: Use of hard-coded password: import_contacts sets every newly imported user's password to the well-known value 'changeme123'. Anyone who knows this default (it also appears in the seed data) can authenticate as any imported customer contact until the password is changed - an authentication bypass for the whole contact-import flow.

Hard-coded insecure default SECRET_KEY: when the SECRET_KEY environment variable is not set, Django falls back to the well-known string 'django-insecure-local-dev-only-change-me'. Deployed without the env var, this allows session-cookie and CSRF-token forgery (session hijacking / CSRF bypass).

Debug mode enabled by default: DEBUG defaults to True when the DEBUG environment variable is unset. In production this exposes detailed error pages, stack traces and settings (CWE-209 information disclosure) and, per lines 97-98, also disables SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE and CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE.

Hard-coded database credentials: the default connection string 'postgres://crmuser:crmpass@localhost:5432/crm_db' embeds a database username and password directly in source code (also mirrored in .env.example).

Hard-coded demo credentials: the seed command creates the platform admin with password 'adminpass123' (and equally predictable passwords for manager/support/customer users, plus 'changeme123' for 19 imported contacts). Running this seed in any reachable environment yields instantly compromisable privileged accounts.
